newsitem.title: USA: CILCORP supports latest restructuring bill.
newsitem.headline: CILCORP supports latest restructuring bill.

text.p: CILCORP Inc said Tuesday it support a new electric industry restructuring bill introduced in the Illinois House with the support of a broad-based alliance representing residential, commercial and industrial consumers.
The utility said the lead sponsors include the co-chairmen of the House Electric Deregulation Committee Kankakee Democrat Phil Novak and Glen Ellyn Republican Vince Persico.
Although the bill differs from one introduced by CILCORP, it "includes the principles we have laid out," spokesman Greg Woith said.

Under the bill, known as the Electric Customer Choice and Protection Act, all electric customer utilities would have the opportunity to buy electricity from their provider of choice beginning May 1, 1998.
Woith said CILCORP, the owner of Central Illinois Light, had sought a January 1 beginning for customer choice.
In November, the Illinois Coalition for Responsible Electricity Choice called for limited customer choice beginning next year and completing the deregulation process statewide in 2005.

The coalition consists of Unicom Corp, CIPSCO Inc, Illinova Corp, MidAmerican Energy Holdings Co, Union Electric Co, Illinois Industrial Electricity Consumers, Chemical Industries Council of Illinois, Illinois Manufacturers' Association and the Illinois Retail Merchants Association.

CILCORP's statement said the latest proposal calls for all customers tol have equal access to a competitive electric market at the same time, with no special treatment for large users. Most consumers could receive up to a 10 percent rate reduction the first year.
More reductions are possible the second and third years.
The coalition proposed a rate freeze for most customers until January 1, 2000, followed by reductions of 1.5 percent annually through 2004.
The latest proposal also says electric service providers must register with the Illinois Commerce Commission, which would continue to regulate transmission and distribution.

It would allow utilities needing additional revenues to ensure financial viability and reliability to participate in a trust fund by charging all consumers on their systems $0.003 per kilowatt-hour used.
To receive disbursements from the trust fund the utility would have to "prove" its need to the commission.
Woith said this replaced securitization in the proposal.

Municipal electric systems and rural electric cooperatives are not required to open their facilities to competition under the legislation. State and local taxes and municipal franchise fees would continue at existing levels.

Assistant Majority Leader Arthur L. Turner, a Chicago Democrat and a lead sponsor, said, "H.B. 1998 appears to be that compromise legislation everyone has been seeking to really start the restructuring debate in earnest."

Novak said, "This consumer alliance bill is a welcome contribution to the electric restructuring debate in Springfield, and the first piece of legislation that has support from major representatives of all three electric customer classes -- residential, commercial and industrial."

Persico said, "While its details still need to be carefully examined, this bill is significant in that it does attempt to address the 12 necessary points identified by the House Deregulation Committee."

Other organizations supporting the legislation include: Citizens Utility Board; Illinois Citizens for a Sound Economy; Art Institute of Chicago; Building Owners and Managers Association of Chicago; Illinois Restaurant Association; Akzo Nobel NV's Akzo Chemical; Caterpillar Inc ; Enron Corp ; General Mills Inc ; Koppers Industries Inc KOP.N ; Nestle SA ; Reynolds Metals Co; RR Donnelly & Sons ; Uno-Ven ; and World Color Press Inc.
